contract.words: I want $6,000 of settled cash within 30 days, and it has to come from independent auto-parts stores — selling to them or doing work for them. I can put in up to $1,000.

terms.proofCondition: First independent auto-parts store pays and cash settles
exclusions: Buyers other than independent auto-parts stores

strategy.title: Sell a one-time $500 local-search package to independent auto-parts stores by phone and email, gated by a 60-store test
strategy.why: 4,317 independently-owned NAPA stores (GPC FY2025 10-K) plus Auto Value/Parts Plus independents give far more buyers than the 13 needed; aftermarket-shop website/local-search vendors publish $500 setup fees (AAM Base $100/mo + $500 setup) and Hibu sells managed listings/reviews to parts stores, so the price is anchored; the owner can fulfil with AI drafting at ~$20 per store, well inside $1,000; card cash settles within the 30 days. What no record shows is whether independent store owners buy this from a cold call at $500 - only a live test measures that.

alternatives.title: eBay Motors listing build of slow-moving inventory ($750 flat)
alternatives.why: No published price that parts stores pay for a listing build, and buyer count of stores with eBay-ready dead stock is unknown; delivery (fitment accuracy, store must photograph/ship) is heavier. Kept as a second offer to pitch to stores that decline the local-search package.

alternatives.title: Monthly managed local marketing retainer ($300/month)
alternatives.why: Only the first month settles in the window, so it needs 20 stores instead of 13; comparable retainers (SimplePart retailer tier, repair-shop agencies) are not measured purchases by independent parts stores.

steps.label: Build a list of 150 independent parts stores (independently owned NAPA, Auto Value, Parts Plus, unaffiliated) from public store locators and Google Maps, noting each store's Google Business Profile gaps; phone/email the first 60 on days 1-5
Offer a one-time $500 local-search package: Google Business Profile optimisation, parts/services posts, review-request QR/SMS link, one-page store site; card payment via Stripe payment link on order
Validation: count paid $500 orders from the first 60 stores contacted by day 10
If proof met, contact the remaining ~90 listed stores and close to 13 paid orders by day 24
Deliver each package within 3 days of payment: optimise the store's Google Business Profile (manager access), publish one-page site (domain + hosting $20 per store), set up review-request link
Collect by Stripe card payment at order; Stripe fee 2.9% + 30c per $500 charge; payouts T+2, a new account's first payout 7-14 days after first payment

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right kind of stance (demand, price and close rate are unknowns only a live test measures), and the arithmetic of the target is sound: 13 x $500 = $6,500; Stripe 13 x $14.80 = $192.40 and domain/hosting 13 x $20 = $260, total $452 inside the $1,000 cap; net about $6,048, just over $6,000. But passing the test at its threshold does not carry the target inside the window: 2 paid of 60 is 3.3%; the plan then contacts the remaining 340 stores at about 25 per working day, which takes ~13.6 working days (about 19 calendar days) from day 11, i.e. to about day 30, not day 24; at 3.3% that gives ~11 more orders only as the window closes, before 3-day delivery and T+2 settlement. At threshold the 400 stores yield 13.3 orders, so there is zero slack even if the time fitted. The cash ledger does not match the steps: it books 13 receipts between day 4 and day 20 (about one per day, 3 by day 8), whereas the steps produce ~2 by day 10 and the rest through day 24+. The test also takes buyers' card payments at order before fulfilment is shown possible (the card's fulfillment is only a RECOMMENDATION that the owner drafts with AI; the stop rule on first-delivery hours fires only after orders are charged). Only the 4,317 count is accepted evidence.

reviews.reasons: The earlier findings are answered. A free pilot package on days 1-2 (stop if over 6 owner hours or $40, or not accepted) proves fulfilment before the first paid offer on day 3, so no store is charged before delivery is shown possible. Price is now ASSUMED, and AAM, Hibu and genpt are matchesBuyer false; only the 4,317 count (accepted) is EVIDENCED. The threshold is 4 paid of 60 (6.7%); over 400 stores that implies about 27 paid, roughly twice the 13 needed, so passing at threshold carries the target with margin. Recomputed: 13 x $500 = $6,500 gross. Stripe fees 13 x $14.80 = $192.40 and domain/hosting 14 x $20 = $280 make $472.40 total spend, inside the $1,000 cap; settled cash after fees is $6,307.60, which clears $6,000 even before netting the domains. The ledger now follows the steps: 4 receipts in the test window (days 4-8), then 9 from the remaining 340 contacts (days 9-20) through day 22, with the first four settling day 18 (new-account worst case of 14 days) and the last on day 26, inside 30. Brain's trace agrees: collected $6,500, spent $472.40, peak exposure $223.60. The buyer restriction (independent auto-parts stores only) is respected. CONDITIONAL with decides [CURRENT_DEMAND, OFFER_AND_PRICE, CONVERSION, FULFILMENT] is the right stance.

strategy.title: Sell a one-time $500 local-search package to independent auto-parts stores by phone and email, gated by a 60-store test
strategy.why: The buyer population is the one established fact: 4,317 independently-owned NAPA stores (GPC FY2025 10-K), far more than the 13 needed. Everything else is measured by the plan itself: a free pilot proves the owner can deliver the package and records its hours and cost before anyone is charged; a 60-store test measures whether independent store owners pay $500 and at what close rate - the price is an assumption (vendors such as Aftermarket Websites and Hibu sell website/listing services to aftermarket shops, but no record shows a parts store paying $500 for this package). Spend is about $480, inside the $1,000 cap, and card cash settles inside 30 days if the last orders close by day 22.

alternatives.title: eBay Motors listing build of slow-moving inventory ($750 flat)
alternatives.why: No published price that parts stores pay for a listing build, and buyer count of stores with eBay-ready dead stock is unknown; delivery (fitment accuracy, store must photograph/ship) is heavier. Kept as a second offer to pitch to stores that decline the local-search package.

alternatives.title: Monthly managed local marketing retainer ($300/month)
alternatives.why: Only the first month settles in the window, so it needs 20 stores instead of 13; comparable retainers (SimplePart retailer tier, repair-shop agencies) are not measured purchases by independent parts stores.
